values: This publication uses Community Services Dataset (CSDS) data to report on monthly 2-hour UCR performance and activity levels for all providers of UCR
services in England. It includes data tables for three metrics:
Table 1: % of 2-hour UCR referrals that achieved the 2-hour standard, per month and per provider, Integrated Care Board (ICB), region and national
Table 2: Count of 2-hour UCR referrals in scope of the 2-hour standard, per month and per provider, Integrated Care Board (ICB), region and national
Table 3: Count of all 2-hour UCR contacts, per month and per provider, Integrated Care Board (ICB), region and national
The publication includes one sheet per key performance indicator and data is presented by organisation (in rows) and by month (in columns). Organisations
included are national, NHS commissioning region, ICB and provider. A new column of monthly data will be added in each monthly publication.
Each month the latest month of provisional (primary) CSDS data will be added and previous months' data will be overwritten with final (refresh) CSDS data.
This ensures data can be made available in a timely manner. There will be changes in performance and activity levels between publication of primary and
refresh data, therefore, caution is advised in the use or analysis of provisional data. Final data, as the most comprehensive and accurate version of the data,
As the publication uses CSDS data, these statistics are classified as experimental and should be used with caution. Experimental statistics are new official
statistics undergoing evaluation. More information about experimental statistics can be found on the UK Statitics Authority website.
If an organisation has not submitted any data relevant to any of the three tables, they will not be listed in the publication.

New technical guidance was published in March 2023 and has been applied to data covering April 2023 onwards.
The main change affecting the data is the expansion of the definition to include any services (such as GP-out-of-hours or district nursing services) that are not part
of an urgent community response service but delivery care that meets the requirements of a two-hour-urgent community response. Therefore, data before and after April 2023
is not comparable and it is not possible to perform trend analysis across these data points.
